title: Broker→renderer governed-turn result (rev-30 §4.10(g))
description: The closed broker→renderer reply frame. Exactly one of committed (carries the broker-produced immutable message projection, NO reason) or blocked (carries a CLOSED reason enum, NO message). Every reply echoes client_request_id and broker_turn_id. UI-safe: no store handle, key, envelope, hash, nonce, or verdict internals. THIS IS THE RENDERER'S ACCEPTANCE CONTRACT, NOT THE BROKER'S EMISSION SET: it describes the frames the renderer accepts, and the broker can emit a committed frame this schema refuses -- see message.trust_state.

trust_state.description: The renderer's acceptance contract, not the broker's emission set. The broker commits a turn under one of two labels and projects whichever the committed row holds (apps/desktop/src-tauri/core/src/governed_message_store.rs: trusted_verified, or demonstration_custody for a chain that ran under a root whose custody proves nothing), so a real broker frame may carry demonstration_custody and fail this const. That is intended. The renderer rejecting every commit that is not trusted_verified is one of the three refusals holding the production gate (CLAUDE.md section 6, the second half of refusal 1: the Bridge panel reaches connect_broker without governed_verification_unconfigured(), and there this pin is what refuses). apps/desktop/src/services/governedTurn.ts refuses a demonstration_custody commit, says a broker verdict existed and was not accepted, and never carries its reply to the screen. Kept a const, not widened to an enum, by Owner decision of 2026-10-02; widening it is the Owner's alone. tools/test_renderer_broker_schemas.py locks both the const and this sentence.
